meta.architecture: pre-LN, causal, GELU MLP, 2 stacked blocks
meta.convention: row-vector: X is (seq, d_in), W is (d_in, d_out), Y = X W. Megatron's convention, so column-parallel really does split W's columns.

backward_steps.label: residual 2 split
backward_steps.note: h2 = h1 + D. Addition sends the gradient down BOTH paths unchanged -- the identity branch is a gradient superhighway, which is why very deep stacks train at all.

backward_steps.label: MLP backward
backward_steps.note: dW2 = G^T dD needs the saved GELU output G; dW1 = n2^T dU needs the saved LayerNorm output. Same outer-product structure as any linear layer, so the same activations must be kept.

backward_steps.label: LayerNorm 2 backward
backward_steps.note: Two correction terms, not just g/sigma. The mean and the variance each depend on every element of the row.

backward_steps.label: output projection backward
backward_steps.note: dWo = O^T dA, where O is the concatenated head outputs saved in forward.

backward_steps.label: attention backward
backward_steps.note: Softmax's Jacobian is dense: dL/ds_i = p_i (dL/dp_i - sum_j dL/dp_j p_j). The subtracted scalar is why every row of dS sums to zero.

backward_steps.label: Q/K/V backward
backward_steps.note: All three read the SAME LayerNorm output, so their input-gradients ADD. One saved tensor, three consumers.

backward_steps.label: LayerNorm 1 backward
backward_steps.note: And the residual adds its untouched copy back in, so the gradient leaving this block is never smaller than the one that entered by the skip path alone.
